title: Device-tiered performance manifest and autopublisher playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a standardized, machine-readable 'device-tiered manifest' format and an automated publish pipeline that turns validated benchmark signatures into runtime-consumable performance manifests for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 variants. The manifest will capture throughput/latency envelopes by sequence length, cold/warm KV footprints, recommended quantization buckets, thermal/hysteresis hints, and fallback compatibility mappings. The autopublisher will run after benchmark ingestion and verification, enforce SLO gates, and emit versioned manifests to the profile registry used by the routing/pinning service.
acceptance_criteria: Define JSON manifest schema that covers performance envelope, cache footprints, quantization guidance, and compatibility tags for A100/H100/L40S/MI300
Implement CI job that validates benchmark signature artifacts and generates a versioned manifest in the profile registry when SLO gates pass
Expose a verification report (HTML) with p95/p99 delta heatmaps and publish/rollback recommendation
Integrate manifest consumer in runtime router so new manifests can be rolled out via canary or immediate pin by model-version
Document playbook and add runbook for manual rollback and emergency softpins
comments: 2026-02-16 — Aisha K.: Initial scoping completed. Decided to opt for a single manifest format (v1) rather than separate files per SKU to simplify registry queries. Will use 'flavor' keys for A100/H100/L40S/MI300.

2026-02-20 — Ethan M.: Prototype schema drafted (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Device+Tiered+Manifest+v1). Key trade-off: include thermal thresholds vs. keep manifest small. Proposal: include thermal hints as optional fields to enable thermal-aware throttles later.
2026-02-25 — Review (Platform Reliability): Schema looks good but request to add 'telemetry_keys' to map manifest metrics back to benchmark buckets for auditability. Added to schema v1.1.

2026-03-01 — Eng Lead (Marina Lopez): Approve autopublisher pipeline approach but require SLO gates (latency p95 drift < +12%, throughput drop < 15%) before auto-publish. Also require an opt-out label for manual publishes for high-risk models.
2026-03-04 — PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1189 — contains manifest producer and registry upload task. CI flows added to pipeline 'bench->validate->report->publish'.

2026-03-07 — QA notes (Ben Chu): Ran end-to-end with sample Llama-2-70b on H100. Publish blocked by thermal hysteresis warning; autopublisher emitted 'manual-review' flag. Action: adjust thermal gating thresholds in validation job and re-run.

2026-03-09 — Ops (Sofia Grant): Canary rollout recipe reviewed. Added SLA-linked rollback hook: if canary p99 latency regresses > 8% or error rate increases > 0.5% within 10 minutes, auto-revert to previous manifest and create incident path.

2026-03-10 — Ethan M.: Implemented registry upload with semantic versioning (manifest-YYYYMMDD-<increment>). Next: wire router to accept 'manifest_source' header to test canary routing in dedicated clusters.
notes: Schema highlights: 'flavor' (string), 'seq_buckets' (list of buckets with p50/p95/p99 strings), 'kv_cold_bytes', 'kv_warm_bytes', 'quantization_recs' (list), 'compat_map' (list of runtime-compatible variants), 'thermal_hint' (optional object), 'telemetry_keys' (list) — all fields must be present as null or concrete to ease validation.

Autopublish flow: benchmark ingestion -> signature validator -> heatmap generator -> SLO gate checks -> verification report -> publish (or manual-review). Publishing writes versioned manifest to profile-registry with provenance metadata (bench run id, commit sha, author).

Rollback considerations: softpin vs hard revert. Softpin reduces new requests routed to the manifest over a configurable decay window; hard revert swaps manifest atomically. Default autopublish uses softpin for first 30 minutes of canary unless SLA curve is stable.

Operational knobs to surface in Console: manual publish toggle, auto-publish enable/disable per model family, thermal sensitivity slider, canary window length, and softpin decay rate. These will be added as follow-ups with PM/Design.

Compatibility: ensure manifests are consumable by Hosted, Dedicated, and Private runtimes. For Private, manifests must include 'signed_by' and 'artifact_checksum' fields to support air-gapped verification.
